//: Example Claude Code hook configuration for dira. Merge these entries into
~/.claude/settings.json (or a project .claude/settings.json) — do not replace
the file, since other tools register hooks here too.
`dira install-hooks` will do this merge for you once the binary exists; this
file documents what it writes, so the wiring is reviewable rather than magic.
It must match the contract kazi's `install-hooks` already proved (cli.ex:440,
ADR-0071/ADR-0076): merge-never-clobber, idempotent, the operator's own hooks
and keys survive byte-identically, `--uninstall` removes exactly what was added,
and `--local` targets the repo's uncommitted .claude/settings.local.json rather
than the user-level file. Clobbering a hand-tuned settings file is a failure
mode kazi already solved; do not rediscover it.
The three hook points are chosen deliberately — see docs/design.md §5.1.
Every command must be fast and must fail open: a dira error must never block
a session. Hence `|| true` on the capture hooks and a hard timeout on all three.
Inversion 2 — review is push, not pull. Injects the brief into Claude's
context so both parties are oriented before the first prompt. --context
renders the agent-facing form; bare `dira brief` is the human-facing one.
--chain walks the tier parents (repo -> workspace -> personal) so a
session in one repo knows the current focus might be elsewhere (§8.2).
Output is hard-capped at 1,500 tokens by cst-0001, enforced in-binary.
Tier-1 capture. Regex-only, offline, deterministic, lossy. Anything it
finds is written `state: staged` with `source.tier: regex` and waits for
disposition — a regex has no business asserting rationale (dec-0003).
--quiet prints nothing when there is nothing staged, so the common case
adds no noise to the transcript.
The insurance policy. Fires immediately before Claude Code's lossiest
moment, so a four-hour brainstorm cannot evaporate into a compaction
summary. --deep runs the same regex pass --stage does, through the same
may-only-ever-stage writer, and additionally emits the handoff block the
semantic tier works from. No API key is involved anywhere (dec-0003).
CORRECTION, dec-0023. This comment used to say --deep 'asks the live
session (via the skill) to fill in the because, the rejected
alternatives, and the derives_from edge'. It cannot, and never could.
PreCompact is not one of the events whose stdout is delivered to the
model, and it carries no hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext. What it
does on exit 0 is append stdout to the COMPACTION SUMMARISER's prompt —
a one-turn call explicitly told that tool calls will be rejected. So the
block's only reader here cannot run `dira log`, and the failure is
silent: everything exits 0 and no entry is ever written. dec-0023 has
the quoted evidence.
What still holds: tier 1 loses nothing. Every candidate the regex pass
finds is staged from this hook exactly as it would be from Stop, which
is what makes this an insurance policy rather than a gamble.
What has to move: the handoff's DELIVERY, not its capture. PreCompact is
the only point at which the about-to-be-compacted transcript still
exists, so the capture stays here. Stop accepts additionalContext and is
already wired above; SessionStart injects context and its matcher list
includes 'compact'. E2-L2 owns choosing between them — until it lands,
read this hook as tier-1 capture that also prints a block, and not as a
working tier-2 handoff.
Longer timeout than the others because this one is worth waiting for,
and it happens rarely.
